done_when: A test fails on old code: a worktree with a fold commit on top of the real work ships the real commit(s) and the pushed range contains no fold-only commit; recorded run of sync.py ship on a scratch repo shows the pushed shas
goal: Gap: the context-fold commit that a hook adds after every Bash call polluted a ship (first ship of the Docker drop pushed only a fold commit). Choose: ship ignores/squashes fold commits, or the hook stops committing on ship worktrees. Default (OURS): the fold goes into the card file inside the real ship commit, never a separate commit. Related: context-gap-fold-on-ship.
note: Related, not a twin: context-gap-fold-on-ship builds the fold; this card stops the fold polluting ships.
scope_out: unrelated files; live tree; other cards
steps: Read the gap text and linked files
Run the test on old and new code; record output
title: Ship ignores or squashes context-fold commits; hook must not commit on ship worktrees
